cands.name: Eric Ching

money.note: Individuals gave $96,920; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Taiwan-born entrepreneur and IT professional who says he served over a decade on the Walnut, California city council, twice as mayor. Graduated from Alhambra High School and Cal State LA (1995). Republican nominee for Congress in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed by Ballotpedia for 2024 and 2026)

Association for LA Deputy Sheriffs (2022 and 2024), LA County GOP, American Independent Party and Pastor Paul Tan of City Blessing Worldwide, as listed in his own 2026 Ballotpedia survey (self-reported)

cands.gaps: We could not independently confirm his years on the Walnut city council or as mayor, or his claim about the city's financial reserves; both come from his own statements. We found no documented actions in office tied to his stated positions. We found no documented stance on data centers, housing or development, homestead property taxes, or limits on investor or foreign land purchases. We found no pledges about donors or foreign-linked money. We found no statement on teacher pay. His statements on immigration do not address H-1B visas. We found no news reporting or controversies about him.

back-police-order.evidence: Said on his campaign website that he wants to be tough on crime and would support laws holding officials accountable who selectively neglect to do their jobs.

money.note: Individuals gave $283,580; PAC money $552,089; candidate's own money $9,194. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Democrat and Navy veteran (supply officer, 1994–2004). Worked as a Frito-Lay logistics manager, then ran a scholarship foundation with his wife after a 2010 lottery win. U.S. Representative for CA-39 (2019–2021), Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (2021–2023), and Representative for CA-31 since 2025.

endorsements.text: 2026 recommendations include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.
2024 endorsements include U.S. Reps. Pete Aguilar and Judy Chu, Democratic Majority for Israel PAC and Reproductive Freedom For All.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Cisneros on data centers or on specific development or rezoning projects. We found nothing on homestead property tax, restrictions on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. The pages we had did not include his 2025–2026 bill sponsorships or actions in office, so we could not show what he did on these issues. His 2026 Ballotpedia candidate survey was not completed, so we have no 2026 questionnaire answers. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the sources we had. Sources disagree on whether he was born in Los Angeles or Torrance.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

clean-money.evidence: His campaign website says he refuses donations from Big Pharma, oil corporations, tobacco, gun manufacturers and private prisons, and supports campaign finance reform and a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United (2024 site).

second-amendment.evidence: His 2024 campaign website says he supports bringing back an assault weapons ban, universal background checks and safe-storage measures, and that he earned an 'F' rating from the NRA.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign website says abortion decisions should stay between a woman and her doctor, and that he opposes the Hyde Amendment and supports repealing the Helms Amendment. It also says he signed a Pentagon policy on reproductive healthcare access for service members.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign website says he supports comprehensive immigration reform with the DREAM Act and a pathway to citizenship, and wants to protect DACA and TPS. It also mentions enhancing border security 'in a responsible and humane manner'.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign website says he will work to keep public lands public and supports conservation of lands and waters.
